MULTI-SECTION EXPORT COMPLETE 2026-08-24. render-markdown.ts#buildRenderMarkdown now emits the full cv-document.ts scheme: `# Name`, the master's own contact line(s), `## Section`, `### Title — Org (Period)`, `- bullet`. Contact detail (email/phone/links) is extracted from the master markdown between the H1 and the first `## ` and re-emitted joined with ` | `, the same separator cv-document.ts splits on, which is what makes the confirmClaim re-render idempotent. Job titles are derived in code by fact-provenance.ts#parseEntryHeading (title, org, and period fall to null together whenever the heading does not clearly split as `Role — Company`) and carried on FactContext / cv_fact.title / FactSnapshot. Entry grouping key is now the (title, org, period) TRIPLE. Both writers verified end to end: extracted PDF text layer and DOCX word/document.xml both contain the contact parts and the titles, and both sha256s are stable across repeated renders.

LinkedIn Description granularity FIXED 2026-08-24: linkedin.importer.ts#splitDescription emits one markdown list item per claim (author's own bullets/newlines win; otherwise a deterministic sentence split that skips decimals, initials, and abbreviations), so a role no longer extracts as one paragraph-sized fact. Known under-split: a sentence ending in a URL path segment ("Visit https://a.b/c. Then...") stays as one claim, because the final token reads as a single-letter initial. Under-splitting keeps a whole claim intact, so it is the safe direction; revisit only if it shows up in real exports.

SCHEMA GAP RESOLVED 2026-08-24. ExtractedFact/ContextualFact/FactSnapshot/cv_fact now carry {section, title, org, period}. Mapping is by normalised text (the same normalisation hashFactContent uses): exact match first, then containment either way with a 12-char floor so a short token like "Py" cannot match an arbitrary line. Where several matching blocks DISAGREE on a field it is nulled per-field, so a bullet duplicated under two employers still keeps its shared section. Unmapped facts are logged at warn with counts and truncated text, never thrown — a heading-less CV is a valid input. Derived context is deliberately OUTSIDE contentHash (pinned by tests in fact-identity.spec.ts and fact-provenance.spec.ts): re-titling a job heading must not orphan every fact under it.

Facts extracted before 2026-08-24 have cv_fact.title NULL (AddFactTitle1756700000000 deliberately does not backfill — a guessed job title is fabrication). They render title-less as `### — Org (Period)` until the master CV is next saved and re-extracted. Not a defect; noted so a title-less entry on an old application is not mistaken for a derivation bug.

Phase 4 export renders one 'Tailored Highlights' section: SUPERSEDED. Exports are now real multi-section CVs with per-entry title/org/period. What is still missing structurally is anything the fact graph does not carry at all — e.g. a location line per entry, or ordering entries by date rather than by first appearance in the bullet array.

EXPORT-FAILURE RECOVERY RESOLVED 2026-08-24. New `POST :id/retry-export` -> ApplicationsService.retryExport. approve()'s `state === 'in_review'` guard is UNCHANGED and stays absolute; recovery went into its own entry point so the guard never grows a conditional a later reader could get wrong. retryExport is gated on all three of: state === 'approved' (never 'downloaded' — the user demonstrably holds a file from that render), stateError set (the marker an export actually failed; without it a retry would be a re-approval through a side door), and at least one of ARTIFACT_KINDS still missing (a complete set means the files may already be in the user's hands, the spec §6.3 divergence). approve() now clears stateError only AFTER export succeeds, so 'approved and exported' and 'approved but export failed' stay distinguishable on the row. A failed retry re-records the error and re-throws — it never tidies the state.

BULLET IDENTITY RESOLVED 2026-08-24. TailoredBullet.bulletId + ConfirmedClaim.bulletId, both OPTIONAL in the type because provenance/confirmedOverreach are persisted jsonb. bullet-identity.ts#bulletIdOf derives `b:<sourceFactId>` when the field is absent, so legacy stored renders resolve identically with NO data migration. sourceFactId is a valid key because TailorService/ReviseService both drop a bullet whose source fact was already used, and it is stable across a confirmClaim re-render and across a reword (a content hash would detach decisions on reword; a positional index would detach on drop). confirmClaim and the approval gate now address bullets by id; the confirm-claim DTO takes `bulletId`, not `bulletText` (BREAKING for any client). ConfirmedClaim keeps bulletText as the audit trail. A legacy ConfirmedClaim with no bulletId resolves by text ONLY when that text is unambiguous in the render — with two identical-text bullets it clears NOTHING and the user re-decides, because silently clearing the wrong twin would approve a claim nobody ruled on.

NUDGE PATH VERIFIED END TO END 2026-08-24. Proven live, not just in tests: a BPCP instance parks on the `sent` signal, the minute-by-minute InstanceTimeoutService sweep fires it on timeout (onTimeout: continue), the dispatcher resolves ${env:CV_NUDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET} into the x-cv-nudge-secret header, cv-tuning's callback authenticates to notifications-microservice with its scoped service token, the send succeeds, and nudgedAt is stamped. A second callback for the same application returns {nudged:false, reason:'already nudged'} — no duplicate email. Exercised with a temporary version 2 of the workflow carrying timeoutMs=60000 and a seeded cv_application row; BOTH were removed afterwards (row deleted, table back to 0 rows; ConfigMap republished with v1 only and BPCP restarted, registry now serves version 1 at 86400000 only). Three real defects were found this way, none of which unit tests could see: a 500 on a non-uuid applicationId, a 401 from missing service-token auth, and a 500 SEND_FAILED from an omitted `channel`.

Phase 6 by decision, not oversight: no revision/chat loop for supplements. ReviseService is CV-shaped (it re-renders bullets into a cv_render) and generalising it is a larger refactor than the phase needs; regenerating produces a new revision, covering the same need at far less risk.

Phase 6 by decision, not oversight: supplements are NOT in the approval gate. `approve` guards the CV artifact the user is accountable for, and widening it would let a cover-letter verdict block a CV export.

PHASE 7 GDPR CORE RESOLVED 2026-08-27. ConsentGuard (src/master/consent.guard.ts) gates CV-processing routes on CURRENT consent (stored version must equal CV_CONSENT_VERSION), applied at method level to master save/imports, job score, and application create/regenerate/revise/confirm-claim/approve/retry-export/cover-letter/screening; it runs AFTER the controller-level CvAuthGuard and reads req.user. Read-only and data-subject-rights routes are deliberately NOT gated. New src/privacy module: GET /api/privacy/export (full graph + artifact bytes/refs), DELETE /api/privacy/account (verified-MinIO-then-transactional-DB hard-delete cascade), POST /api/privacy/retention (expire cv_job.rawText past expiresAt keeping parsed; purge orphaned artifacts), POST /api/privacy/reconcile (offboarding). MinioService gained deleteObject (DELETE then HEAD-verify) and objectExists. No migration — every column already existed.

PHASE 7 OFFBOARDING BLOCKED 2026-08-27 (not an oversight). Offboarding reconciliation (OffboardingService.reconcile) is implemented but BLOCKED at runtime: auth-microservice emits no offboarding events AND exposes no user-listing/existence API, so there is no authoritative 'this account is gone' signal. The check goes through IdentityProviderPort (src/privacy/identity-provider.ts) behind the AUTH_USER_LOOKUP_URL seam; with no lookup configured reconcile() returns {status:'blocked'} and purges nothing. It NEVER deletes on an unresolved/null lookup — only a positively CONFIRMED-gone (404) account is purged — so an auth outage cannot cascade into deleting a live user's data. Unblocks only when auth grows a user-existence endpoint. Do not fabricate one.

PHASE 7 DELETE/RETENTION ORDERING is load-bearing: the MinIO object is deleted and VERIFIED gone (MinioService.deleteObject does DELETE then a HEAD that must 404) BEFORE the DB row that references it. A row deleted while its object lingers is an unreferenced orphan (unrecoverable); an object deleted while its row lingers is recovered by re-running the idempotent cascade. The hard-delete cascade and purgeOrphanedArtifacts both follow object-before-row; do not reorder them.

PHASE 7 published sub-processor list is docs/privacy/subprocessors.md (OpenRouter, Google, Anthropic, self-hosted MinIO from spec §9). DPA URLs are [MISSING: authoritative DPA URL] placeholders on purpose — a guessed DPA link is a compliance claim the project cannot stand behind. Replace only from an authoritative source.

pdf-parse's bundled pdf.js throws inside Jest's node environment for ANY PDF (verified with a bare jest config, no ts-jest or Nest involved). Production is unaffected. cv-pdf.service.spec.ts shells out to a child node process to assert extracted text — anyone calling pdf-parse live under Jest will hit this.

pdfkit's built-in Helvetica is WinAnsi-only: CJK, emoji, and Arabic silently corrupt in PDF output. CvPdfService now RAISES on unencodable characters, naming them and pointing at DOCX (which renders them correctly). Real Unicode font support is deferred — needs an embedded TTF, a licence decision, and a Docker image change.

pdfkit hashes info.CreationDate into the PDF /ID trailer, so an unpinned CreationDate makes the sha256 wall-clock dependent. It is pinned to new Date(0) because spec §6.3 reuses that sha256 for artifact idempotency.

LinkedIn Positions.csv Description routinely contains newlines inside quoted fields. Reading the CSV line-at-a-time shredded such a row into a phantom extra position (`### Role — <prose fragment>`) — a job the candidate never held, invented by the parser. parseCsv now splits records via splitCsvRecords (quote-aware); never reintroduce a body.split(/\r?\n/) there.

cv_fact.section/title/org/period are DERIVED IN CODE from the markdown headings (src/master/fact-provenance.ts), never asked of the extraction model, and never part of contentHash. Do not add them to fact-extractor.service.ts OUTPUT_SCHEMA or SYSTEM_PROMPT: a model naming the employer or date range fabricates on the fields an employer judges a CV by (spec 6). Null means "could not be confidently mapped" and must render as nothing downstream — never fall back to a nearby heading.

A tailored entry with NEITHER title, org, nor period still emits a bare `### —` heading. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: cv-document.ts attaches a bullet to the most recently opened entry, so an unattributed group written with no heading of its own after `### Senior Developer — Acme (2019-2024)` is read as more of Acme's work — a real employer and role stamped onto a bullet the fact graph never connected to it. Caught by a test in render-markdown.spec.ts; never 'simplify' the bare heading away. Both writers suppress it (they emit a heading only when a title or org is present), so it never reaches the PDF/DOCX page.

buildRenderMarkdown ordering is deterministic BY CONTRACT: sections, entries, and bullets are all ordered by first appearance in the bullets array, with the 'Additional Highlights' catch-all forced last; the facts array is a lookup only, so its order cannot influence the bytes. Spec §6.3 reuses the artifact sha256 for idempotency, so a Map/object iteration whose order could vary would defeat pdfkit's pinned CreationDate just as thoroughly as a wall-clock timestamp. Pinned by tests in render-markdown.spec.ts.

buildRenderMarkdown's contact block is re-extracted from its OWN prior output on the confirmClaim path, so the emitted form must be the canonical one: parts trimmed, whitespace-collapsed, and joined with ` | ` on a single line between the H1 and the first `## `. Any other join (a different separator, one part per line, a trailing space) makes pass 2 differ from pass 1 and silently changes the artifact sha256 spec §6.3 depends on. Pinned by a three-pass test in render-markdown.spec.ts.

A derived job title is user-authored text written into a `### ` heading, so render-markdown.ts#normalizeHeadingField collapses its whitespace and rewrites any em dash to a hyphen before emitting. An em dash inside a title would make cv-document.ts re-parse `### Lead — Deputy — Acme (2019)` as an ambiguous heading and silently relabel the employer; a newline would break the one-heading-per-line parse. Neutralised rather than dropped — losing a real title is a silent loss, mangling the employer is a fabrication.

Entry grouping is keyed on the (title, org, period) TRIPLE, not (org, period). A promotion inside one company over the same period is two real CV entries; keying without the title merged them and discarded one job title. Nulls are values in that key, not wildcards: a title-less bullet never joins a titled entry at the same employer.

TailoredBullet.bulletId must NEVER reach cv_render.markdown or either export writer: spec §6.3 reuses the artifact sha256 as artifact identity, so leaking an internal id would change the hash for logically identical content, exactly like an unpinned CreationDate. buildRenderMarkdown takes only text/sourceFactId. Pinned by bullet-id-artifact-stability.spec.ts, which asserts through the real PDF and DOCX writers, not by string-matching.

bulletId is derived, never generated. Read it through bullet-identity.ts#bulletIdOf, never as `bullet.bulletId` directly — a raw read sees undefined on every render already in the database. Never switch it to a uuid or a content hash: derivation from sourceFactId is the whole reason stored rows stay decidable without a migration.

The nudge callback POST /api/nudges/outcome is NOT under CvAuthGuard: BPCP's ActionDispatcherService posts plain JSON with no user credential, so a user-token guard would reject every call. It is protected by the x-cv-nudge-secret shared-secret header (CV_NUDGE_CALLBACK_SECRET, from Vault) and by the service having no ingress before Phase 7. Never 'fix' it by adding CvAuthGuard — that silently disables every nudge, and the failure appears only as instances stuck in BPCP.

The outcome nudge sends BEFORE stamping nudgedAt, deliberately. Stamping first would mark a nudge delivered that never left the building and the user would never be asked again; sending first means a crash between the two can at worst nudge twice. Duplicate nudges are recoverable, a silently-lost one is not.

BpcpClientService returns null for a missing base url; NotificationClientService RAISES for one. Not an inconsistency: an unset BPCP url means 'this deployment has no workflow plane', a valid configuration, while an unset notifications url is only ever reached when a nudge is already due, so it means a promised notification is being dropped.

The dashboard funnel is CUMULATIVE (each stage counts everything at or past it) and interviewRate is null, never 0, when nothing has been sent. A 0% rate over zero submissions reads to the user as 'your CV is failing' when the honest answer is 'no data yet'.

In-cluster service names verified 2026-08-24: the workflow plane is business-process-control-plane:3375 (NOT 'bpcp'), notifications is notifications-microservice:3368. A wrong hostname in k8s/configmap.yaml fails only at runtime, with every test still green.

BPCP's workflow registry is IN-MEMORY and was hardcoded at construction — there is no create route on its registry controller, so the plan's 'POST the definition to /api/processes' does not exist. cv-tuning's workflow reaches BPCP as the bpcp-workflow-seeds ConfigMap, mounted read-only at BPCP_WORKFLOW_SEED_DIR=/etc/bpcp/workflows and loaded once at boot. Editing docs/workflows/ therefore needs `scripts/publish-workflows.sh` AND a BPCP restart; a commit alone changes nothing in the cluster.

The nudge callback validates context.applicationId as a uuid BEFORE the lookup. cv_application.id is a uuid column, so a malformed id reaches Postgres as a cast error and surfaces as a bare 500 'Internal server error' — which BPCP then retries three times as a transient failure, because 5xx is classified transient. Found 2026-08-24 by a live smoke test that used a non-uuid correlation key. Never relax the check: 'malformed request' must stay a permanent 4xx so BPCP stops retrying it.

notifications-microservice requires a Bearer token and its HS256 self-minting path is RETIRED (RS256 only, jwt-verifier.ts TASK-KEY-F3 step 4), so cv-tuning CANNOT mint its own token the way AiClientService does for ai-microservice. It authenticates with a scoped static service token instead: NOTIFICATIONS_SERVICE_TOKEN, stored once at secret/prod/cv-tuning and referenced by BOTH ExternalSecrets, resolved on the far side as the machine actor `service:cv-tuning`. Never point this at SERVICE_TOKEN — that one grants global:superadmin. Found 2026-08-24 when the first real nudge came back 401.

notifications-microservice requires an explicit `channel` on /notifications/send whenever `channelKey` is omitted (channel-registry.service.ts#resolveSendPolicy). Omitting both is NOT a 400 from the DTO — it passes validation and fails later as a 500 SEND_FAILED, which BPCP then classifies as transient and retries. The outcome nudge sends channel:'email'.

cv-tuning was the only one of 41 deploy.config.sh repos with no .git/hooks/post-commit, so no commit here ever queued a deploy (Phases 1-4 must have been deployed by hand). The mechanism is per-repo by design — shared/scripts/deploy-queue/install.sh symlinks .git/hooks/post-commit in each repo; there is no core.hooksPath set globally. Fixed 2026-08-24 by symlinking to shared/scripts/deploy-queue/post-commit-hook.sh, identical to the other 40. If a fresh clone ever deploys nothing, check for that symlink first.
EntailService.validate() is now shared by THREE generators (TailorService, CoverLetterService, ScreeningService). A change to its signature has three call sites, not one.

renderToDocument() does NOT raise on cover-letter markdown — it silently collapses the whole letter into contact.parts, which both writers render as one header blob. Supplements must go through renderToSupplementDocument().
Screening verdicts are re-attached to questions BY INDEX, never by sourceFactId: EntailService returns verdicts in input order, and two questions may legitimately cite the same fact.

ParseIntPipe accepts '1.5', '1e3', '0' and '-1'. Supplement revision numbers are validated with an explicit /^[1-9]\d*$/ before any lookup, because a malformed segment reaching Postgres is a bare 500 that callers retry.
